QVQU.note: Correct same-parity rule (odd or multiple of 4), but listed 24 as not divisible by 4; counted 7 instead of 6.

SQXU.note: Uses (a-b)(a+b) with same parity; finds the six 2 mod 4 exceptions. Wording muddled midway but ends right.

BRKX.note: Derives odd or multiple of 4, then miscounts: omits 24 from multiples of 4, gets 12-5=7.

JGTD.note: Cites known not-4k+2 result without deriving it; counts 2,6,10,14,18,22 correctly.

CKCM.note: Sets n=xy with same parity, states not-2-mod-4 criterion after false starts; counts 6.

MVCT.note: Parity argument: even n needs 4 dividing n; odd works. Counts six 2 mod 4 numbers after long verification.

ABTH.note: Expands powers of 2+i, splits real and imaginary parts, solves linear system to (5,-24,42).

SZJD.note: Direct expansion and real/imaginary system; a=5n, b=-24n, c=42n; gcd forces n=+-1.

CEVW.note: Direct expansion and linear system; parametrises solutions; gcd condition gives |c|=42.

QKVF.note: Direct expansion and linear system; c=-42m, m=+-1, so |c|=42.

MYDW.note: Direct expansion and linear system; c=42m; gcd forces m=1.

SUBV.note: Direct expansion, solves system, verifies (5,-24,42) in the original equation.

CRJE.note: Shift to Q=P+x+3 with roots a,b,c; Q=k(x-a)(x-b)(x-c); k=2 from P(-3). Fixed an arithmetic slip by checking.

TFZY.note: Early shifts muddled; final route reduces P(a) using a^3=-3a^2-5a-7, matches coefficients, A=2 from P(-3).

FEVW.note: Shifted by x+1 not x+3, so Q does not vanish at a,b,c; asserted Q=k(x-a)(x-b)(x-c) anyway; never found k or P.

FCGQ.note: Sets P+x+3=k(x-a)(x-b)(x-c) but claims k=1; P(-3)=-8 contradiction; blames a typo; answers x^3+3x^2+4x+4.

GEGB.note: Q=P+x+3 has roots a,b,c; (3+a)(3+b)(3+c)=8 gives k=2; expands to gold and checks.

RFVT.note: Same shift and factor form; k=2 via f(-3)=-8; expands to 2x^3+6x^2+9x+11 and verifies.

EUUQ.note: Muddled start, then long brute-force over squares with listing errors; never uses n+1111=b^2 or factors 1111; no answer at cap.

RHPJ.note: Gets n'=n+1111 but drops the condition that n is square; takes k=46, n=1005 without checking or factoring.

AWGF.note: Long muddled search; only n' treated as square; answers 3114 (n+1111=4225) though 3114 is not square. No factoring.

NKPH.note: Lists squares as n', subtracts 1 per digit; accepts 3114 without requiring n square. No factoring.

FZFY.note: Confused framing, but ends enumerating square n with digits below 6, adding 1 per digit; finds 2025 to 3136. Brute force.

JTUZ.note: Same misread: squares enumerated as n', digits minus 1; accepts 3114 without checking n is square. No factoring.

KQBY.note: Factors a_n=n((n-1)!+1) and a_{n+1}=(n+1)(n!+1); general analysis muddled; answer 2 rests on small-n checks.

EKTR.note: Small-case gcds plus a flawed parity argument; no (n-1)(n+1) reduction visible. Reaches 2 by pattern, not proof.

QUEU.note: Wrongly derives gcd=1 for all n, then corrects with small cases n=0..9 and answers 2. Empirical, no key factoring.

XWSH.note: Euclid step B-(n+1)A=-(n+1)(n-1) gives gcd(A,(n+1)(n-1)); n-1 coprime; checks n+1 part and n=100; answer 2.

UCMV.note: Uses difference n(n!+1); a miscalculation gave gcd 6, later corrected; ends with small cases and prime checks. Weak argument.

TRTW.note: Long small-n gcd table, muddled parity and prime-divisor analysis; no reduction to gcd(a_n,(n-1)(n+1)) visible; no answer at cap.

DZTD.note: Factors x^3+x^2-20x=x(x+5)(x-4), clears denominators, matches coefficients: G=1, H=2.

VNXA.note: Factors denominator, equates numerators, matches coefficients: G=1, H=2.

VZNQ.note: Factors denominator, common denominator, coefficient matching gives G=1, H=2.

RTYF.note: Factors denominator, equates numerators, coefficient matching gives G=1, H=2.

EGEN.note: Factors denominator, equates numerators, solves G=1, H=2; one stray remark but result right.

GNTW.note: Factors quadratic via formula, common denominator x(x-4)(x+5), equates numerators; G=1, H=2.

SKQT.note: Missed the cube; used x=sqrt2*y, factored cubic in y correctly, then back-substituted wrongly (+-(sqrt2/2)i instead of +-i).

TUSB.note: Ansatz (x+a*sqrt2)(x^2+bx+c) gives a=1; coefficient check failed, then substitution x=sqrt2*y fixed it; correct roots.

TSPV.note: Guessed root -sqrt2 but synthetic division wrong (5sqrt2 not 3 as constant); never saw the cube; messy wrong complex roots.

UAVN.note: Gets (x+sqrt2)(x^2+2sqrt2x+3) correctly, but reports only the real root; omits -sqrt2+-i from the final answer.

XSQU.note: Tests candidate roots, finds -sqrt2, divides to (x+sqrt2)(x^2+2sqrt2x+3); complex roots -sqrt2+-i.

QPMC.note: Guesses root -sqrt2, long division, quadratic formula; all three roots correct.

PPXN.note: Closed form (n(n+1)/2)^2 gives 231^2=53361; units digit 1. The alternative route.

MABS.note: Sums unit digits of cubes (45+45+1=91), then cross-checks with closed form 53361.

TXPZ.note: Closed form checked on n=1,2; computes 231^2=53361; units digit 1.

DRBJ.note: Closed form gives 53361; cross-checked by summing unit digits of 21 cubes (91).

QFJA.note: Lists all 21 cubes, sums unit digits to 91, answer 1. Pure enumeration.

item_notes.olympiadbench:2912: Almost all use (a-b)(a+b) with same parity. Both failures miscounted multiples of 4 below 25 (dropped 24), giving 7. Correct responses reach 2 mod 4.
item_notes.math:intermediate_algebra/train/00691: All six expanded the powers of 2+i, split real and imaginary parts, and solved the linear system. No factoring needed; all correct.
item_notes.math:intermediate_algebra/train/00918: Winners shift to P+x+3, factor k(x-a)(x-b)(x-c), find k from P(-3). Failures: wrong shift (x+1), or assumed k=1 and blamed the problem.
item_notes.omni:omni/03629: Four of six forgot n itself must be square and returned 3114. One capped on brute force. None used b^2-a^2=1111; the only success used enumeration.
item_notes.math:number_theory/train/00126: Only XWSH reduced to gcd(A,(n-1)(n+1)). Others reached 2 by small cases with flawed general arguments. TRTW capped in an unfocused search.
item_notes.math:algebra/train/01030: Routine: factor denominators, clear fractions, match coefficients. All six correct.
item_notes.math:intermediate_algebra/train/00004: No one saw (x+sqrt2)^3. Successes used root guess or substitution then division. Failures: arithmetic back-substitution, bad synthetic division, dropped complex roots.
item_notes.math:number_theory/test/00090: All six used the closed form or unit-digit enumeration. None used the pairing factorization. All correct.
